# Functional normal-cone injection and simultaneous cap profiles

This is a functional version of the proved finite-support injection in
`candidate 5fcdb1b3fadb0891`. It retains one
common baseline set and the complete incidence profile of several caps.
It does not select an OC center or replace the midpoint factor by Gamma.

## 1. Functional injection

Let A,B be nonempty compact subsets of R^m, let V be a linear subspace,
and let Z=V+conv B. Suppose H_q(A)<infinity, q>=0. Let F:R^m->[0,infinity)
and g:A->[0,infinity) be bounded Borel functions such that

    F(a+b)>=g(a) for every a in A and every b in B.       (1)

Then

    integral_((A+B) minus Z) F dH_q
                   >= integral_(A minus V) g dH_q.       (2)

The left side may be infinite. Boundedness is convenient but unnecessary:
the same proof works with nonnegative Borel functions and extended
integrals. No measurability assertion for an arbitrary uncountable
pointwise infimum is needed: g is explicitly assumed Borel.

Proof. For epsilon>0 use the finite actual support set, distinct projected
vertices, fixed lifts, and smallest-index maximizing rule of the cited
injection. Applied to A_epsilon={a in A:dist(a,V)>=epsilon}, it gives a
finite Borel partition E_i and disjoint translated images E_i+b_i inside
(A+B) minus the ORIGINAL cylinder Z. The proof uses support error
 delta<epsilon and gives the strict gap

    ||pi a||*(||pi a||-delta)>0.

Injectivity includes ties: maximizing inequalities give
 (v-w).(p_i-p_j)>=0,
whereas coincident images give v-w=-(p_i-p_j); the one-lift convention
then forces the same original point. Consequently translation invariance
of Hausdorff measure gives

    integral_((A+B) minus Z) F
      >=sum_i integral_(E_i+b_i) F
       =sum_i integral_(E_i) F(a+b_i) dH_q(a)
      >=integral_(A_epsilon) g dH_q.

Taking epsilon=1/j and applying monotone convergence to the increasing
SOURCE sets proves (2). There is no limit of maps, target sets, or selected
points, and no assertion that a single limiting map exists on all A.
For V=R^m the right side is zero; the case q=0 is the same finite point
argument. If A,B lie in the mixed lattice, each actual translation
preserves it exactly, including all boundary mass and all intrinsic q.

## 2. A single baseline set is retained additively

Let P be any compact subset of A contained in an affine subspace L.
Translate A,P,L by the same vector so that L becomes linear, while
leaving B fixed and translating the argument of F accordingly. Formula
(2), together with P+B subset L+conv B, implies

    integral_(A+B) F dH_q
      >= integral_(P+B) F dH_q
                    + integral_(A minus L) g dH_q.        (3)

The two terms are charged to disjoint target regions. In particular,
when q=d is ambient volume and dim L<d, the second term is integral_A g.
This is a statement about one baseline P+B. It must not be repeated for
several different baselines and added as if their new target mass were
disjoint.

## 3. Actual simultaneous missed-cap profiles

Let A,B,K be d-dimensional convex bodies with (A+B)/2 subset K. Let
v_1,...,v_s be fixed normals satisfying v_i.b<=1 for every b in B.
Let P be one compact subset of A whose affine span has dimension less
than d. Define the Boolean vectors

    sigma(x)_i=1_{v_i.x<0},
    rho(a)_i=1_{v_i.a<-1}.

Every actual sum satisfies sigma(a+b)>=rho(a) coordinatewise. Let
Psi:{0,1}^s->[0,infinity) be ANY coordinatewise nondecreasing function.
Applying (3) with F=Psi(sigma) and g=Psi(rho), then using the homogeneous
zero-level cuts under the dilation by 1/2, gives the exact joint bound

    2^d integral_K Psi(sigma(x)) dx
      >= integral_(P+B) Psi(sigma(x)) dx
                              + integral_A Psi(rho(a)) da.   (4)

This holds for every such Psi with the SAME actual body and baseline
hull P. It involves the actual cap-intersection areas or volumes, not
only the individual cap masses. All strict boundaries have been retained;
for ambient d-volume they are null, but no deletion is needed in the
injection proof. Replacing < by robust compatible weak inequalities is
also legitimate when those are the incidences intended.

For a mixed-integer midpoint version, require that the actual source
sets lie in one common integer parity class so that every chosen midpoint
belongs to the lattice. Use H_q, retain the mass on L if necessary, and
replace 2^d by exactly 2^q. No Gamma factor follows from this rescaling.

## 4. Explicit union, intersection, and multiplicity consequences

For an index set I write

    G_I^union = union_(i in I){x:v_i.x<0},
    E_I^union = A intersect union_(i in I){a:v_i.a<-1}.

The choice Psi(s)=1_{some i in I has s_i=1} gives

    2^d |K intersect G_I^union|
      >= |(P+B) intersect G_I^union|+|E_I^union|.          (5)

The analogous AND function gives the same inequality for intersections.
In particular the common residual-hull additive theorem is an AND
specialization with its separately proved lower bound for the baseline
hull. The present union version retains a different joint quantity.

More generally, put N_I(x)=sum_(i in I)1_{v_i.x<0} and
N_I^A(a)=sum_(i in I)1_{v_i.a<-1}. For any integer ell>=0, the increasing
function Psi=(N_I-ell)_+ gives

    2^d integral_K (N_I-ell)_+
      >= integral_(P+B) (N_I-ell)_+
                               + integral_A (N_I^A-ell)_+.  (6)

Thus overlap multiplicity above a chosen level is charged to the same
baseline plus actual source overlap, using one translation partition.
Weighted maxima and other increasing Boolean profiles are also allowed.

These formulas are not obtained by summing marginal halfspace bounds:
such a sum controls N_I but discards its distribution. For example,
on an abstract two-bit profile the law placing equal masses at 00 and
11 has the same two coordinate means as the law placing equal masses
at 10 and 01, while their AND masses are 1/2 and 0 and their union masses
are 1/2 and 1. This elementary example explains the extra information
retained by (4); it is not asserted to be a convex-body construction.

## 5. A residual-profile specialization and its exact limits

For canonical positive-circuit normals v_0,...,v_d with sum v_i=0,
put

    R_j(A)=A intersect intersection_(i!=j){v_i.a<-1},
    R_j(K)=K intersect intersection_(i!=j){v_i.x<0}.

Within either family these regions are disjoint. For any set J of k<=d
nonempty actual R_j(A), choose P_j in each one and put P=conv{P_j:j in J}.
Then dim aff(P)<=k-1<d, and every P_j+B lies inside the corresponding
R_j target in sum coordinates; those translates are disjoint and each
has volume b=|B|. Applying (4) to the indicator of the union of these
AND profiles yields

    2^d sum_(j in J)|R_j(K)|
                     >= k b+sum_(j in J)|R_j(A)|.          (7)

One can use any larger target index set containing J on both residual
sums, while retaining k b from the selected baseline translations.
Formula (7) is a correct joint-profile consequence, but on its own it is
weaker than summing ordinary Brunn--Minkowski over the separate convex
residual sets. It is not promoted as a new closure mechanism. The useful
additional information in (4) is the full actual baseline integral and
the freedom to use other overlapping/union profiles; obtaining a sharp
lower bound for those joint baseline integrals remains a separate task.

None of (2)--(7) proves that a given profile must occur in a hypothetical
OC counterexample, and none supplies a missing all-direction center.

## 6. Exact planar critical residual-profile budget

In the actual three-fiber planar setting, let v_0+v_1+v_2=0 be the
canonical independent-direction circuit, B subset T, and suppose the
three ambient cuts v_i.x-z>=0 all have raw mass Q. Write a=|A|, k=|K|,
and U_i=|A intersect {v_i.x>=-1}|. B contributes zero area, so the own
middle captured masses are Q-U_i. Outside the finite union of boundary
lines, the number N_K of missed middle caps is either one or two.
Therefore

    integral_K (N_K-1)_+=2k-3Q+sum_i U_i.

On A the robust missed count is at most two, and its positive excess
above one is precisely the indicator of the union of its three disjoint
unique-capture residual regions R_i(A) defined in Section 5. Thus for
ANY one compact P subset A of affine dimension at most one, (6) gives

    4[2k-3Q+sum_i U_i]
       >= sum_i |(P+B) intersect intersection_(j!=i){v_j.x<0}|
                                             +sum_i |R_i(A)|.   (8)

The target intersections in the baseline sum are disjoint. Equation (8)
retains their ACTUAL shared-hull geometry; its first sum is not replaced
by a formal collection of independently realizable tail values. This is
a fully explicit joint critical-cap consequence of the functional lemma.
It does not assert a lower bound for that sum beyond what the actual
geometry or separate proved hull results provide, and it is not itself
a closure of the remaining planar branch.

## 7. One absent planar corner gives an upper bound for its middle residual

Let d=2 and v_i+v_j+v_k=0 be the canonical three-normal circuit. Suppose

    B subset T={v_l.x<=1 for l=i,j,k},   (A+B)/2 subset K,
    R_i(A)=A intersect {v_j.x<-1,v_k.x<-1} is empty,
    R_j(A) and R_k(A) are nonempty.

Choose deterministic actual P_j in R_j(A), P_k in R_k(A), and the ONE
baseline segment P=[P_j,P_k] subset A. Define

    G={v_j.x<0} union {v_k.x<0},
    E=A intersect ({v_j.x<-1} union {v_k.x<-1}).

The two source sets in this union are disjoint by the absent-corner
hypothesis. Hence, writing U_l=|A intersect {v_l.x>=-1}| and a=|A|,

    |E|=2a-U_j-U_k.                                      (9)

Every actual translation of E by B lies in G. We will prove the strict
shared-baseline estimate

    |(P+B) intersect G|>2b,     b=|B|.                   (10)

Indeed put B_j=P_j+B, B_k=P_k+B, and w=P_k-P_j. Every point of B_j
strictly misses normals i,k and hence has v_j>0. Every point of B_k
strictly misses normals i,j and hence has v_k>0. Thus these two compact
translates are disjoint, belong to G, and each has area b. In particular
v_k is strictly negative on B_j and strictly positive on B_k. Put

    eta_j=-max_(x in B_j) v_k.x>0,
    delta=min{1/2, eta_j/[2 v_k.w]}>0.

The denominator is positive: v_k.P_k>2 whereas v_k.P_j<-1. The actual
short sweep B_j+[0,delta]w is contained in P+B and in {v_k<0}, because
its v_k maximum is at most -eta_j/2. It is disjoint from B_k, on which
v_k>0. Elementary line-section integration parallel to w gives

    |B_j+[0,delta]w|
       =b+delta J_B(w),
    J_B(w)=||w|| H_1(proj_(w perpendicular) B)>0.

Each nonempty line section grows by exactly delta||w||; the transverse
projection is unchanged. Thus this is an exact area identity, with the
Euclidean factors tracked, and not an assumed disjointness of overlapping
sweeps. We have proved the stronger baseline estimate

    |(P+B) intersect G|>=2b+delta J_B(w).              (11)

Now use the union transfer (5) with this same P. Combining (9)--(11),

    4|K intersect G|
       >=2b+delta J_B(w)+2a-U_j-U_k
        >2b+2a-U_j-U_k.                              (12)

The injected added source mass lies outside the cylinder of the whole
baseline segment, so it is disjoint from BOTH portions used in (11).
Only one baseline and one injection occur.

In the exact three-fiber critical setting of Section 6, the middle
captured volumes are Q-U_l. Put

    r_i^K=|K intersect {v_j.x<0,v_k.x<0}|.

Inclusion-exclusion in K gives

    |K intersect G|=2k-2Q+U_j+U_k-r_i^K.

Consequently the missing source corner imposes the actual joint bound

    4 r_i^K
       <=8k-8Q+5(U_j+U_k)-2a-2b-delta J_B(w)
        <8k-8Q+5(U_j+U_k)-2a-2b.                     (13)

This is an upper restriction on a SPECIFIC middle residual region, whose
corresponding residual in A is absent. It retains a strictly positive
actual geometric term from the selected segment and B. Marginal
halfspace inequalities do not retain this intersection term. Replacing
r_i^K by only a scalar union-bound lower estimate can lose this extra
geometry and is not claimed to close the remaining branch. The points
P_j,P_k and their positive term are actual; no uniform quantitative
lower bound on delta J_B(w) is assumed.

An exact actual-body check for Section 7 uses v_i=(-1,-1), v_j=(1,0),
v_k=(0,1),

    A=conv{(4,-2),(-2,4),(0,0)},
    B=T=conv{(1,1),(1,-2),(-2,1)},
    K=(A+B)/2,
    P=[(4,-2),(-2,4)].

All three A cuts are proper; R_i(A) is empty because x+y>=0 throughout
A, while the other two residual regions are nonempty. Here a=6, b=9/2,
|E|=1, |(P+B) intersect G|=15, and |(A+B) intersect G|=53/2. The explicit
short-sweep term delta*J_B(w) equals 3/2. These values follow by rational
polygon clipping in `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_absent_corner_union_transfer_slab_recovery.py`,
which passes 28 exact checks across four actual compatible examples.
They verify the geometric identity and inequalities, not criticality:
no displayed cap in this calibration is asserted to attain raw depth Q.
